status: Local source repair validated; publication pending
area: Governed commit / candidate attribution and rollback isolation
finding: Ordinary task commit selection treated every dirty tracked actor registry as an implicit attribution dependency, admitting unrelated staged and worktree changes outside the candidate's explicit authority. Taskless preparation could stage the registry again, and the hook independently rejected an isolated candidate for excluded worktree drift. Failure review also found that outer index rollback restored a global snapshot and could overwrite foreign staging created during a failed commit.
expectedBehavior: Resolve registry membership and identity against the exact candidate and canonical current claim, ticket and lane authority. Preserve excluded registry paths as whole files without splicing rows or weakening bare-commit checks. Closed publication slices must exclude unrelated registry state even when it is already staged. Rollback may restore only operation-owned index entries that still match their expected post-write state, under Git's index lock; concurrent writes and foreign locks must survive.
evidenceOrRepro: tests/cli/git-commit-attribution-isolation.test.ts failed red when a foreign partially staged registry entered the sealed candidate, then passed real governed-wrapper commits with a bound-session attribution hook, concurrent foreign staging during failure, exact index/worktree preservation, retry, and framework preview/apply. candidate-attribution.test.ts covers absent/unborn registry state, strict claim/ticket/lane rejection, staged-versus-worktree identity, missing and replayed runtime identity, and author mismatch. Publication-slice tests cover already-staged explicit registry scope and early missing-attribution rejection. Live-index tests cover CAS retention, foreign index locks and rollback rename failure. The CI sweep also caught the hook orchestration exceeding its existing 600-line budget; the complete candidate dependency check was extracted into the cohesive attribution helper, and hook-extraction, physical-line-budget and RFT checks pass without raising the cap.
followUp: Complete independent review and fresh combined build, standard checks and installed acceptance before source publication. Source repair, frozen-runner publication and npm release are separate outcomes. Runtime identity is supported only with exact actor binding and independently valid current candidate authority; excluded uncommitted actor metadata cannot supply it.
